items.title: When Should LLM Agents Forget? Memory Filtering Under Query-Critical Resolver Errors
items.summary:
arXiv:2611.17338v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM memory systems often delete facts classified as stale. We show that this hard-filtering step can reduce downstream accuracy when resolver errors delete query-critical facts. Across three models, a controlled sensitivity intervention moves hard-drop from gains of +0.186 to +0.230 at perfect resolution to losses of -0.176 to -0.181 at the lowest tested reliability. items.reasoning: This is directly relevant to how Meevo might build persistent memory for business assistants. It warns that hard-deleting 'stale' facts can lose information a later query depends on, so soft filtering is the safer design. It is academic research with no effect on Claude API pricing or capabilities, but competitors with tuned memory systems could gain a small reliability edge.
